scenes.visual: Title card: How Many Mice?

scenes.tts: Three hundred units, recorded from three mice. How many samples is that?
scenes.caption: 300 units, recorded from 3 mice. How many samples is that?
scenes.visual: Three hundred small dots appear, then gather under three mouse icons. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: 300 units, recorded from 3 mice. How many samples is that?

scenes.tts: Units recorded from one mouse share that mouse: its genes and its drug dose.
scenes.visual: One mouse icon with its dots inside; small tags appear around it: genes, drug dose.
scenes.narration: Units recorded from one mouse share that mouse: its genes and its drug dose.

scenes.tts: Units recorded in one session also share that day's alertness, and one probe track. If that mouse or session is unusual, its units tend to shift together.
scenes.visual: A session box inside the mouse, with tags: alertness that day, probe track. Its dots shift upward together. Caption: illustrative model, a shared shift.
scenes.narration: Units recorded in one session also share that day's alertness, and one probe track. If that mouse or session is unusual, its units tend to shift together.

scenes.tts: Take a small invented dataset. Two mice. Mouse A gave four units, and mouse B gave two.
scenes.visual: Two columns of dots under mouse A and mouse B, four and two units. Each dot shows its rate on screen: 8, 2, 4 and 8 spikes per second for mouse A, 2 and 2 for mouse B.
scenes.narration: Take a small invented dataset. Two mice. Mouse A gave four units, and mouse B gave two.

scenes.tts: Pool every unit, and mouse A counts twice as much, only because it gave more units.
scenes.visual: A bar labelled pooled mean appears, 4.33 spikes per second on screen, leaning toward mouse A's column.
scenes.narration: Pool every unit, and mouse A counts twice as much, only because it gave more units.

scenes.tts: Average within each mouse first, and each animal counts once. The animal mean comes out lower.
scenes.visual: Mouse A's dots merge first into session means of 5 and 6, then into a mouse mean of 5.5; mouse B's merge into 2. A second bar labelled animal mean, 3.75 spikes per second on screen, sits beside the pooled bar.
scenes.narration: Average within each mouse first, and each animal counts once. The animal mean comes out lower.

scenes.visual: The two bars, 4.33 pooled and 3.75 animal mean, hold on screen with the mouse means beneath them.

scenes.tts: For a claim about mice, the sample is two, not twenty four.
scenes.caption: For a claim about mice, the sample is 2, not 24.
scenes.visual: Large text: n = 2 mice, not 24 unit-trials.
scenes.narration: For a claim about mice, the sample is 2, not 24.

scenes.tts: Now a harder test. Suppose a drug does nothing at all, on average.
scenes.visual: Three mouse icons with before and after columns; a caption reads: true drug effect, zero. Caption: invented variances.
scenes.narration: Now a harder test. Suppose a drug does nothing at all, on average.

scenes.tts: Record a hundred units from each of three mice. Treat all three hundred as independent.
scenes.caption: Record 100 units from each of 3 mice. Treat all 300 as independent.
scenes.visual: A hundred dots fill each mouse; then all the dots pour into one big pile labelled n = 300.
scenes.narration: Record 100 units from each of 3 mice. Treat all 300 as independent.

scenes.tts: How often will a standard test call the drug effect significant?
scenes.visual: The question appears as on-screen text over the pile of dots.
scenes.narration: How often will a standard test call the drug effect significant?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: In a simulation with invented numbers, about seven times in ten.
scenes.caption: In a simulation with invented numbers, about 7 times in 10.
scenes.visual: A grid of 100 symbols standing for percentages, not for the number of simulated experiments; about 68 turn red under the heading: units as n. Caption: illustrative model, 3 mice x 100 units, independent normal shifts, mouse SD 1, unit SD 2, two-sided t-test at 5%, 300,000 simulated experiments.
scenes.narration: In a simulation with invented numbers, about 7 times in 10.

scenes.tts: The same test on the three mouse averages was significant only about five times in a hundred.
scenes.caption: The same test on the 3 mouse averages was significant only about 5 times in 100.
scenes.visual: A second grid of 100 symbols, again standing for percentages, under the heading: mice as n. About 5 turn red.
scenes.narration: The same test on the 3 mouse averages was significant only about 5 times in 100.

scenes.tts: That is the false-alarm rate the test is built to give, when its assumptions hold.
scenes.visual: The second grid is circled; a label reads: nominal 5% rate, test assumptions met.
scenes.narration: That is the false-alarm rate the test is built to give, when its assumptions hold.

scenes.tts: Counting units as independent made the error bars far too narrow. This is called pseudoreplication.
scenes.visual: Two error bars around zero: a narrow one for units as n, a wide one for mice as n. Label: pseudoreplication.
scenes.narration: Counting units as independent made the error bars far too narrow. This is called pseudoreplication.

scenes.tts: Are more units worthless, then? No. They average out the noise between units within each mouse.
scenes.visual: A curve of error against units per mouse falls steeply at first.
scenes.narration: Are more units worthless, then? No. They average out the noise between units within each mouse.

scenes.tts: But no number of units averages out the differences between mice. The error stops shrinking at a floor.
scenes.visual: The curve flattens onto a dashed horizontal line labelled floor.
scenes.narration: But no number of units averages out the differences between mice. The error stops shrinking at a floor.

scenes.tts: With the spread between mice held fixed, only more mice lower the floor.
scenes.visual: More mouse icons slide in; the dashed floor line drops. Caption: fixed variances; floor = mouse SD / square root of the number of mice.
scenes.narration: With the spread between mice held fixed, only more mice lower the floor.

scenes.tts: So report every level, and say which level your question is about.
scenes.visual: A diagram builds: sessions inside animals; within each session, a grid with units as rows and shared stimulus presentations as columns, one observation at each crossing. Label: units and trials crossed within a session.
scenes.narration: So report every level, and say which level your question is about.

scenes.tts: Each of these numbers is a step from your claim. Count your sample at the level of the claim.
scenes.visual: The boxed rule from the first film returns, with the units-to-animals row highlighted.
scenes.narration: Each of these numbers is a step from your claim. Count your sample at the level of the claim.

scenes.tts: And none of this shows that a pathway is needed. That takes a manipulation.
scenes.visual: A small caption reads: needed for behaviour? Test with a manipulation.
scenes.narration: And none of this shows that a pathway is needed. That takes a manipulation.
